purpose: Bounded source-image inspection of two previously withheld part-1 review rows, selected before image retrieval to look for one damaged-name correction and one unreadable/abstention control.

cases.name: washington
cases.raw_text: bill (S. No. 380) to incorporate the AVash- ingt(jn County Horse Railroad Company
cases.visual_finding: The registered crop visibly reads 'Washington County Horse Railroad Company'; the printed word wraps as 'Wash-' / 'ington'.

cases.name: miscellaneous-appropriation
cases.visual_finding: Contrary to the pre-image unreadability hypothesis, the registered crop visibly reads 'remarks on the miscellaneous appropriation bill' followed by dot leaders and page 4288.

findings: The first case is a distinct image-grounded damaged-name reading that supports Washington in this source line, while preserving the original OCR and without assigning a person or changing canonical text.
The second selected row is not an unreadable-image control: its image resolves a fuller index entry. This negative selection result is retained rather than relabeled as an abstention case.
Neither result proves a model can transcribe the cases, supports automatic correction, or establishes a corpus-wide error rate.
limitations: Two part-1 index-like lines are not a representative all-five-part sample.
No vision model or human-review packet was used; these are agent visual diagnostics from source-registered crops.
The text following the dot leaders is transcribed as a visual aid only; exact punctuation/spacing is not promoted to a canonical patch.
A future abstention/control case must be selected and frozen before image retrieval; do not reuse the resolved miscellaneous-appropriation row as unreadable evidence.
registration: IIIF receipts, source/page hashes, exact native-pixel regions, image hashes, and code hashes are retained in each case bundle; no inferred scaling or rotation.
